steps.headline: The lower settings are now one Rules list: a plain label on the left, its value as a pill you click to change.
steps.changed: N-lower ("very convoluted … unclear what these labels/buttons mean"): the tab strips, dropdowns and three separate boxes became five rows in the same style as permissions. A choice that needs words (another time, other instructions) opens a box under its row.
steps.notice: The Notifications card is gone: system notifications are built later, all together (your Q-notify-menu answer).

steps.path: Automation details → Permissions → Add a permission
steps.headline: Each permission you add becomes one exact rule, given only to that job's runs.
steps.changed: "See the files in a folder: ~/Downloads" lets it read inside Downloads and nowhere else. "Run one command: du -sh ~/Downloads" allows that exact command, no other. "Visit one website: bestbuy.com" reaches that site only. "Read this page's information" works on that page only.
steps.notice: Gmail and other services appear in this menu once step 5's sign-ins exist; until then it lists this page, your computer and the internet.
steps.risk: The step after picking a folder, website or command (typing which one) is still not drawn; it will be on the deck after the build.

steps.headline: A job starts with none of your chats' permissions, and nothing a job is allowed ever reaches a chat.
steps.changed: Claude jobs start Claude Code in its restricted mode, which ignores the settings files your chats use and gets only this job's rules, folders and tools. ChatGPT / OpenRouter jobs give YouCoded's assistant the job's list in place of a chat's.
steps.notice: So an "Always allow" you clicked in a chat never applies to an automation, and the other way round.

steps.path: What happens when a run tries something
steps.headline: Every action a run tries lands in one of three places: allowed, asks first, or not on the list.
steps.changed: On the list as Always allowed: it happens. On the list as Asks first: the "Asks first items" rule decides (wait for you, or skip it). Not on the list: "Other websites" or "Other commands and files" decides (Never refuses it, Asks first treats it like an Asks first item).
steps.notice: Example: the price watch lists bestbuy.com; trying amazon.com is "not on the list", so with Never it's refused, the run carries on, and its run box says what was refused.

steps.path: Permissions → Other websites / Other commands and files
steps.headline: Combine "Other websites" and "Other commands and files" into one row: "Anything not listed"?
steps.today: Two rows decide what happens to things not on the list: one for websites, one for your computer.
steps.problem: Two rows for one idea adds to the clutter, and most jobs want the same answer for both.

options.label: One row
pros: One fewer row; the idea reads at once.
cons: A job that should ask about websites but refuse commands can't say so.

options.label: Keep two
pros: Websites and your computer can be treated differently.
